module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 13

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/

@[expose] public section


namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture13

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 13](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph `G`, the size `b(G)` of a largest induced bipartite subgraph
satisfies `b(G) ≥ diam(G) + max_{v ∈ V} l(v) - 1`, where `diam(G)` is the diameter
of `G` and `l(v) = indepNeighborsCard G v` is the independence number of the
neighbourhood of `v`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture13 (G : SimpleGraph α) (h : G.Connected) :
    letI maxL := (Finset.univ.image (fun v => indepNeighborsCard G v)).max' (by simp)
    (G.diam : ℝ) + (maxL : ℝ) - 1 ≤ b G := by
  sorry

-- Sanity checks

/-- The largest induced bipartite subgraph invariant `b G` is nonneg for any graph. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) : 0 ≤ b G := Nat.cast_nonneg _

/-- In `K₂`, all vertices have degree 1, so `indepNeighborsCard` at vertex 0 is 0
(the neighbourhood of 0 consists of only vertex 1, which has no independent edges). -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)).maxDegree = 1 := by decide

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture13

findings.description: The docstring of the second sanity check says: "In `K₂`, all vertices have degree 1, so `indepNeighborsCard` at vertex 0 is 0 (the neighbourhood of 0 consists of only vertex 1, which has no independent edges)." That is false. The neighbourhood of 0 in K₂ is {1}, and a one-vertex graph has independence number 1. I proved in Lean that `indepNeighborsCard (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) 0 = 1` (unfold, `rw [indep_num_eq_computable]`, `decide`). The docstring also talks about "independent edges", which confuses the notion. The example itself only checks `maxDegree = 1` and never tests `indepNeighborsCard`. The main theorem and its definitions are unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: WOWII definition 4 (wowIIdefs.js, web.archive.org capture 20230901203307 of http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/wowIIdefs.js): "local independence of a vertex, λ(v): The independence number of the subgraph induced by the neighbors of vertex v." For K₂ this is 1. The Lean definition `indepNeighborsCard G v := (G.induce (G.neighborSet v)).indepNum` gives 1 too, verified by `decide` after `indep_num_eq_computable`.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring to "In `K₂`, the maximum degree is 1." (as GraphConjecture16 already does), or add a real test: `example : indepNeighborsCard (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) 0 = 1 := by unfold indepNeighborsCard; rw [indep_num_eq_computable]; decide` (this compiles).

reformulations.difference: The section variable adds `[Nontrivial α]` (at least 2 vertices). The source says "If G is a simple connected graph", which also covers the one-vertex graph K₁.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Mathlib's `Connected` requires a nonempty vertex type, so the only connected graph the hypothesis excludes is the single-vertex graph. There `G.diam = 0` (`ediam_eq_zero_of_subsingleton`). Every neighbourhood is empty, so every `indepNeighborsCard` is 0 and `maxL = 0`. Since `b G ≥ 0`, the inequality reads −1 ≤ b(G) and holds trivially. The converse direction is immediate because `Nontrivial` implies `Nonempty`. In a scratch file I proved `(∀ α [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α] G, G.Connected → ineq) ↔ (∀ α [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] G, G.Connected → ineq)` for α : Type, and checked that the file's `conjecture13` instantiates the left side.

DeLaVina and Waller 2004'; the notes to #16 and #19 use #13 as proved. The live site's HTTPS port was unreachable from the sandbox.)

https://web.archive.org/web/20230901203307/http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/wowIIdefs.js (definitions 4 = local independence λ(v), 14 = diam(G), 15 = bipartite number b(G); conjecture 13's reference entry: DeLaVina & Waller, 'On Some Conjectures of Graffiti.pc On the Maximum Order of Induced Subgraphs', Congr. Numer. 166 (2004) 11-32; status codes T/F/R = resolved, O = open, E = exercise)

Numerantium 166, 11-32 (2004). Its summary defines the bipartite number as the maximum order of an induced bipartite subgraph.)
review.notes:
The main theorem `conjecture13` states the source's claim faithfully:
- λ(v) is `indepNeighborsCard`, the independence number of G[N(v)] with open neighbourhood `neighborSet`.
- diam(G) is Mathlib's `diam`, the true diameter because G is connected and finite.
- b(G) is `largestInducedBipartiteSubgraphSize`, the maximum order of an induced subgraph that is `Colorable 2`.
- The inequality is taken in ℝ, and `max'` is over all vertices.

Tests I ran:
- An exhaustive C brute force over all connected labelled graphs on 1–7 vertices (1.87M graphs at n = 7) found no violation of `diam + max λ − 1 ≤ b`. Equality holds for many graphs (min slack 0), so the formal bound has no off-by-one either way.
- 244k random connected graphs on 8–12 vertices (sparse trees plus extra edges, and random densities) also gave no violation.
- Lean spot checks: b(C₅) = 4; λ = 3 at the centre of K₁,₃; λ = 2 on C₅; λ = 1 at vertex 0 of K₂.

Status: `research solved` agrees with the rendered WOWII page ('T', DeLaVina and Waller 2004). The site's older JS data file still lists #13 as 'O', but that file is visibly stale: #15 and #16 there also disagree with the rendered page.

I downloaded the DeLaVina–Waller paper from https://web.archive.org/web/20100701022251/http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/GPC/maximum_induced_subgraphs.pdf, but it is a scanned image with no text layer and there is no OCR tool here, so I could not read its proof. Faithfulness is settled against the WOWII statement and definitions, which the paper cites.
